subsystems.name: Engram identification
subsystems.role: finds the small set of neurons that together hold one memory and can later reactivate it.

subsystems.name: Genetic targeting
subsystems.role: gives a tool only to the cells of interest, so nothing else is switched.

subsystems.name: Molecular switch
subsystems.role: makes those cells controllable by an external signal.

subsystems.name: Delivery and access
subsystems.role: gets the signal to deep brain structures such as the hippocampus without damaging tissue.

subsystems.name: Read-out and control loop
subsystems.role: decodes ongoing activity and triggers stimulation at the right moment.

subsystems.name: Safety and verification
subsystems.role: proves the edit is specific, lasting and does not damage nearby circuits.

buildSteps.title: Record the memory
buildSteps.detail: Electrodes or imaging record which neurons fire while an animal forms or recalls a specific experience.

buildSteps.title: Tag those neurons
buildSteps.detail: A viral vector carrying an activity-dependent promoter drives a marker or switch only in cells active during that window.

buildSteps.title: Verify specificity
buildSteps.detail: Histology confirms the tool landed in the right cells in structures such as the hippocampus, and nowhere harmful.

buildSteps.title: Test reactivation
buildSteps.detail: Light or a drug is applied; if the animal behaves as though the memory returned, the ensemble is confirmed.

buildSteps.title: Test suppression
buildSteps.detail: Inhibiting the same ensemble during recall is used to check whether the memory can be silenced without erasing unrelated ones.

buildSteps.title: Translate to a non-genetic method
buildSteps.detail: For humans, genetic modification of brain cells is the central obstacle, so effort shifts to focused ultrasound, electromagnetic or pharmacological modulation.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: Decoding hardware detects the memory's signature in real time and delivers stimulation only when that pattern appears.

buildSteps.title: Validate clinically
buildSteps.detail: Controlled trials in conditions such as post-traumatic stress disorder would measure symptom change against sham treatment.

prerequisites.why: memory ensembles have been manipulated in rodents, but human engrams cannot yet be located reliably.
viral gene therapy is approved for some diseases, but not for altering memory circuits.
focused ultrasound and related methods are early-stage; optogenetics needs light inside the skull.
coarse categories can be read from brain activity, not the detailed content of an episodic memory.
procedural skills are spread across motor circuits; no evidence exists that a skill can be written in.

pathway.milestone: rodent studies label, reactivate and silence specific fear memories
pathway.unlocks: proof that a single memory has a manipulable physical trace.

pathway.milestone: non-genetic, deep-targeted modulation in animals and early human safety work
pathway.unlocks: a route that does not require editing a patient's brain cells.

pathway.milestone: clinical trials targeting traumatic memories, alongside existing reconsolidation-based therapy
pathway.unlocks: evidence on whether dampening a memory helps real patients.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop memory editing and any form of skill insertion
pathway.unlocks: therapeutic control of intrusive memories — skill transfer remains speculation, and the ethical questions are unresolved.
